abstract: The present report is that of a 40-year-old woman admitted with hematemesis and epigastric pain. Endoscopy revealed a fungating mass in the lower esophagus. Esophageal brushing revealed clustered and single malignant cells with ample cytoplasm, large bizarre nuclei and prominent, irregular nucleoli; the chromatin was irregular with clumping at the nuclear borders. Giant multinucleated malignant cells were numerous. These cells had nuclear molding and abundant acidophilic cytoplasm. Autopsy findings included a large tumor in the lower esophagus and metastases to lung, liver and kidneys. Microscopically, the fungating esophageal tumor and metastases were composed of cyto- and syncytiotrophoblastic elements. Choriocarcinoma of the esophagus is a rarity, and only two cases were found in the literature. The diagnosis, however, can be achieved by brush biopsy since the characteristic cyto- and syncytiotrophoblastic cells can be readily identified, provided that the possibility of this ectopic occurrence is recognized.
abstract_ja: 40歳の女性が吐血と心窩部痛で入院した。内視鏡検査で下部食道に外向性の腫瘤を認めた。食道擦過細胞診では、大きな細胞質、大型の奇怪な核、目立つ不規則な核小体を有する悪性細胞が集簇または単独で認められた。核クロマチンは不規則で核縁に凝集していた。多核巨細胞が多数見られ、核の圧排変形と豊富な好酸性細胞質を有していた。剖検では下部食道の大きな腫瘍と肺・肝・腎への転移が認められた。組織学的には、食道の外向性腫瘍と転移巣は細胞栄養膜および合胞体栄養膜成分から構成されていた。食道絨毛癌はまれであり、文献上2例しか見当たらなかった。しかし、この異所性発生が認識されていれば、特徴的な細胞栄養膜細胞および合胞体栄養膜細胞は容易に同定できるため、擦過生検により診断が可能である。
